calls.head: Don’t buy Kochetkov’s slump against the Capitals
calls.body: Kochetkov has been shaky against the Capitals since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.

calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Hurricanes
calls.body: The Capitals’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Hurricanes’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Capitals tonight. surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Svechnikov has two goals and an assist as the Hurricanes get past the Capitals
paras: Justin Holl made his Capitals debut, after playing for the Blues. Boone Jenner opened the scoring for the Capitals midway through the first. Andrei Svechnikov tied it 1-1 for Carolina early in the second, and the goal stood after the Capitals challenged for goalie interference. The Hurricanes’ Taylor Hall left in the second period and didn’t return. The next day, he was ruled out with an upper-body injury. Holl restored the Capitals’ lead early in the period, and that was all they would get. Eric Robinson tied it 2-2 for Carolina late in the period. Svechnikov scored his second of the night on the power play with just over six minutes left to put the Hurricanes ahead for good. Mark Jankowski added the empty-netter with a minute and a half left to make it 4-2. Svechnikov added an assist for a three-point night.

The Hurricanes had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Capitals 35-22. Pyotr Kochetkov made 20 saves for the Canes, and Logan Thompson stopped 31 of 34 at the other end. The Hurricanes improved to 6-1-1, still first in the NHL in points, while the Capitals dropped to 3-3-0, slipping to fifth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Hurricanes are rolling: six straight wins.
Mark Jankowski has scored in five straight games.

The season series is even at 1-1.
